fix(colour): the door's ✖ keeps the contrast its red has on its ground at lower depths, never lifted to the quiet floor (brandon-unfiled-3248.692p) (#681)

* fix(colour): the door's ✖ keeps its truecolor contrast at lower depths, never lifted to the quiet floor (brandon-unfiled-3248.692p)

keptOn floored its lower-depth contrast at the quiet floor for a reason
that no longer holds: grounds are named shades, not repaired ones. The
floor only acted on the accepted farthest-red case, where it let rounding
pick a non-red that clears 3:1. The floor is now min(text floor, held),
and the comment states the reasons that hold of named grounds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(colour): keptOn names its floor as the red on this ground unrounded, and an empty search is loud (brandon-unfiled-3248.692p)

The floor is measured on the ground the cell is drawn on at this depth,
which can be another rung than truecolor would press the door into, so
"what the red has in truecolor" misread it. Comment, design doc and
colour memory now say "on this ground before rounding".

The `?? fg` fallback covered a search that cannot come back empty: with
the floor at most 4.5:1, truecolor accepts fg itself and every lower
depth draws black and white, one of which stands >= 4.58:1 off any
ground (0 misses over 120,000 random pairs at three depths). It now
throws, naming the floor and ground, instead of silently drawing fg.

The new unit case pins that the faint red is kept as itself, not only
that its contrast lies in a band.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(colour): keptOn's invariant names the depths it holds at, and its throw names the depth and drawn ground (brandon-unfiled-3248.692p)

Black and white are drawn at 256 colours and ansi, not at every lower
depth rich-js has: the Windows console table holds neither, so the claim
is scoped to the depths a colour setting draws at. The error now names
the depth and the ground as drawn, the one the floor was measured on.
The comment says outright that `bg` is the ground this depth draws the
door on, which can be another rung than truecolor's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(colour): the ✖'s hue is held only by the choice among named reds, and keptOn's wording drops "in truecolor" (brandon-unfiled-3248.692p)

The colour memory now names the trap the code hides: rounding and
keptOn's repair measure contrast alone, so at ansi the ✖ can be drawn
silver, yellow or purple. The new unit case's title and keptOn's comment
say "before rounding" like the rest of the change, and the comment is
reflowed.

docs(doctor): the gate comparison's completeness and the unproven count said as they hold (brandon-unfiled-3248.qo8j)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(doctor): settled repositories ride the config row's text in either verdict (brandon-unfiled-3248.qo8j)

A declined repository named only in a failed verdict's notes vanished
from the bar while the row failed. It now rides the reason after the
first problem, as it rides the note after the chain, so the bar and the
CLI name it whatever the verdict and neither counts it. The doctor's log
keeps unproven worktrees in a field of their own, since each is also
awaiting or declined.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(doctor): a repository answer during the probes refuses a stale report; settled lines count as no problem (brandon-unfiled-3248.qo8j)

The landing compares the gate by its lines, so an awaiting repository
declined mid-run with the config unchanged gathers again. A failed
verdict carries notes beside its problems, so a declined repository is
listed by the CLI and counted by neither the bar's row nor the log. The
doctor's log line carries the gate's counts, and one empty-gate fixture
serves every test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(doctor): the config row names a repository config the load left out (brandon-unfiled-3248.qo8j)

The doctor's config load now carries the repository gate it ruled, so the
config row says why a project's .cc-candybar.json5 is not in the chain. A
repository awaiting approval fails the row and names its directory. A
declined repository, and a directory whose worktree claim is unproven, ride
the row's text without failing it: only reversing the user's own answer
would clear a declined one. repoGateLines is split into the awaiting and
the settled lines, so check, the demo and the doctor share one wording.

An unread answers book already reaches the row as the load's own advisory,
so the doctor takes the awaiting lines alone and names that notice once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Merge 3b55367aa1bd4f969c02da4fc771b790f07cdfd5 into 1f5014d66591bcdbb9dac6e5fb1aa8619e0bf5fd

fix(update-act): a look stages its spend in the act's own directory, never making one (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

writeAtomic made the act's directory when a newer claim had pruned it,
flushed every 2 s look on the render loop, and staged at a name shared by
every daemon. A look now stages at a pid-named file inside the act and
renames it, unflushed: an act gone under the look spends nothing. The
concurrent-writer safety no longer waits on writeAtomic's staging change.
Reverts a formatter reflow of test/update-act.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(update-act): a look spends at most five polls, and a spend it can't read is an error (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

A dark wake mid-sleep spent the 60 s cap, so forty of them overnight ended
the act and could tear the bundle; the cap now follows the poll interval,
in the watch that owns both. awake.json is parsed: a missing number read
as NaN, compared past the budget and ended a running build. Corrects the
race comment: concurrent looks lose nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(update-act): an act's budget is the time it was watched running, so a sleep does not end it (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

The update act was ended once the wall clock passed the deadline in its
record. Wall time runs while the machine sleeps, so closing the lid mid-build
for longer than ten minutes signalled the build's group at the first tick
after wake, possibly mid-write, which tears the bundle.

The budget is now spent in observed time: each tick that finds the act's group
alive adds the span since the last look, whichever daemon took it, capped at
60 s, into the act's awake.json, and the act ends once that passes ten
minutes. A sleep of any length spends at most the cap, a clock set back spends
nothing, and daemons looking in turn or restarting mid-act share one budget.
The record keeps its deadline for older daemons reading the same acts during
an update.

Merge 4ebec8cd99703f75802b334ac8cdfd5108e776a1 into 1f5014d66591bcdbb9dac6e5fb1aa8619e0bf5fd

test(state): the cross-process writers are waited on by name and never outlive the case (brandon-unfiled-3248.wkh1)

Medium review of #678. The wait for both writers to exit goes through the
shared poll helper and names each child's state, the sampling stops with the
case, and the case kills both children on the way out. A child's exit code
is what judges it, with its stderr carried for the reason. stagedPath's
marker says it is this runtime's one spelling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(state): every staged write names a staging of its own (brandon-unfiled-3248.wkh1)

High review of #678. The staged name adds a random part beside the pid, so
two writes never share one whatever they share (a process, a pid namespace),
and it lives in a module of its own that every stage-then-publish site uses:
writeAtomic, the session state file, the socket lease, the fork-bomb
registry, the link key, the pricing cache and a job's end status. A failed
flush removes its staged file. The cross-process test's children wait on a
pipe the test holds, name a failed spawn, and the reader no longer spins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(state): concurrent writers of one file stage at their own names (brandon-unfiled-3248.wkh1)

Two processes sharing a state directory both staged a write at
`<file>.tmp`, so one's rename published or moved the other's bytes and
the other's rename failed ENOENT. Every staged name now carries the
writing process's pid, spelled once by `stagedPath` in
src/utils/atomic-write.ts: writeAtomic, both session-state-file stages
and the socket lease use it. The fork-bomb breaker stages by an
injected identity's pid and is left as it is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(demo): the bundled sample draws the default's session cell and no doubled padding (brandon-unfiled-3248.0d5a)

The sample re-derived the default's session-id cell without its `when`,
so an empty id drew a bare glyph; it now places the default's
`sessionId`. Its templates padded cells the layout already pads. The
bundled-sample test now also fails on a loader advisory naming the
sample and on a drawn warning indicator, not only on a refusal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(demo): `pnpm demo` loads and renders its bundled sample (brandon-unfiled-3248.0d5a)

The sample declared `model` and `session` input variables, under which
the bundled default's `model.display_name` and `session.*` sit, so the
loader's no-nesting check refused it and `pnpm demo` exited 1. The
sample now reads the default's names instead of redeclaring them, and
the demo test runs the bundled sample so it cannot drift from the
loader again.

Merge 8a317cdb45d51bdfbdadf65eaa9e628150310556 into 2e9ea2dce98b1908a16f3ffa2128310350ebc817

fix(state): a set key is reserved as spelled, and the domain ⚠ says what the bar draws (brandon-menus-sjhy.46w)

The loader refused an authored `set` whose key only collapsed like one under
a reserved namespace (`edit-mode`, `menus_open`), though a session key is
compared as spelled and can never meet a synthesized one. The refusal now
asks the spelled namespace, the one `isReservedName` already asked.

The domain warning said the bar draws the key's default, but a stale
placement draft falls to the saved value and a stale setting to the file or
preset. It now says the bar draws as if nothing were picked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(lanes): the session-pane draw composes its view with the state gates the daemon hands it (brandon-menus-sjhy.46w)

The rebase onto main brought in a test that builds a session view without
the state gates this branch's view now judges by.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(state): a reserved key has only its control as writer, and a never-rendered session judges nothing (brandon-menus-sjhy.46w)

Answers /code-review high on 068bb06a (dispositions on PR #676).

- The loader refuses an authored `set` whose key is in a reserved
  namespace, so a placement draft's gate is its declaration's and its
  parse at the render cannot refuse what the gate admitted.
- A session with no recorded render origin has no config: its judged
  read judges nothing instead of throwing inside a write's closing view.
- The keyspace epoch is a MobX atom, so a computed judging through a
  gate re-evaluates on a daemon-wide register or dispose.
- toolbar-toggle reads toolbar-expanded judged; save-theme-default's
  release read is raw, as every release read is.
- The demo and check judge and gate with one Gates each.
- The cycle, ring and standing-warning comments say what holds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(state): a session value its config no longer admits draws the default and warns (brandon-menus-sjhy.46w)

Session state outlives the config that wrote it. A stale value was swallowed
silently: the globals resolution dropped it, a placement's bar drew the saved
value while its carousel sat on its first option, and a carousel or cycle
folded an author key's stale value to its first member.

- The gate judges a stored value (Gate.verdict): a key one of the config's
  own `set` actions writes, holding a value its validator refuses or changes,
  is foreign. A key no `set` writes is the daemon's own and is held.
- JudgedState (src/daemon/foundations/judged-state.ts) is the branded reader
  every interpretive reader demands: the registry's `state` variables, step-
  state (which now steps from the seed instead of clamping), the verbs'
  settings picks, the closing view's closeNested, and the idle close's
  openRoots. Back admits a value only if the verdict holds it. Release reads
  after a reload stay raw.
- session.foreign (the session view) lists foreign values; the draw stands one
  amber `domain` warning per key, identified by its key.
- The ring shows a held non-option between the last and first options; the
  cycle keeps its rest-first reading, with the reason stated.
- validateBoolean accepts its own canonical false, "".
- placementSetting drops its fallback for a refused draft.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cache): each catch-up turn takes the most recently used due entry as the map stands (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A session drawn during the walk is now re-read on the next turn, not
where its entry stood when the batch began. A turn clears its handle
before it reloads and arms only when none is armed, so a batch started
inside a turn leaves one walker. A throw is logged with its stack.

fix(cache): a catch-up turn is its own error boundary and walks most recently used first (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A walk turn runs from setImmediate, outside the watcher registry's
try/catch, so a reload that threw there reached uncaughtException and
shut the daemon down. The turn now logs the throw and arms the next.

The walk takes the most recently used entry first, so the bar in front
of the user is re-read on the first turn. The due set is a Set: every
due entry always reloads for the latest batch's cause, which the armed
turn carries.

fix(cache): a catch-up reloads one entry per turn, so requests are answered between entries (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

When file events resumed after a stall, or the repo answers moved, the
render cache reloaded every entry in one synchronous turn. A reload that
keeps its state still resolves, validates and keys the whole chain, so
105 entries held the live daemon's loop for 1.7s on a calm machine and
11s on a loaded one, and every client waiting behind it hung up (the
EPIPE bursts in daemon.log).

The walk now takes one due entry per turn of the loop. Any reload clears
its entry's due mark, a drop clears a dropped entry's, a reload that
throws ends only its own turn, and close cancels the armed turn. The
render cache's stats count the entries still due.

Merge 9cfce78aed5fb0edc8a096e2bb32236ce4bc81e0 into d8be82f47dab2890d335b8563bbfdc937aedba77

fix(config): undo puts a click's text back on the disk the click wrote; a write's stat error is never a cleanup's (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- The settings history takes the daemon's disk, and the config text read and
  write take a disk: a click, its proof, its write and its undo are one
  disk's. config-file-store leaves the systemFilesystem owners.
- writeAtomicOn takes the replaced file's mode before the tmp exists, so a
  stat that fails is the error the caller sees.
- config.md: ENOTDIR counts as absent beside ENOENT.

fix(config): a click writes its home on the disk it read and proved; the book's folder is absent as presence says (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the click's writable disk; the commit writes through it
  (writeAtomicOn), so a click's read, proof and write are one disk's. Undo
  keeps its own system-disk pair until the settings history takes a disk.
- bookIsFiled asks presence(): a book folder that is a regular file holds no
  book, and the loose book is read.
- holdsGit asks presence() and marks its no-silent-failure exception; the
  ascent carrying the failure is candybar-testing-ihvy.izc.sv9.

fix(config): a click's proof shares the render cache's installed layers and reads its home's disk (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the installed-layer memo its loads share; the render
  cache lends its own through the verb context, so a click's proof checks no
  plugin the bar's last load already checked. The memo keys on definition
  text, so a lent memo serves no layer the borrower's disk does not hold.
- presence() reads ENOTDIR as absent, as the stat it replaced did: a path
  through a regular file holds nothing. The filesystem contract pins ENOTDIR.
- A click reads its home's text and the layers above on the disk its proof
  loads; config-file-store leaves FS_READERS.
- The lane edge's fileExists asks the same disk as its presence.
- stateFromLoad folds into loadFromDisk; keyLoad is module-private.

feat(config): a renderer loads config as a value over the filesystem port (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

Every read a config load makes goes through the FilesystemReads it is
handed: the answers book, discovery, worktree links, plugin folders, each
layer and each definition. readConfigLoad (src/config/load.ts) is the load
as a value; the render cache builds state from it. Each definition is read
once per load, and the installed-plugin memo is an owned value keyed on
the texts, not module state keyed on a stat. The answers book's read moves
into Config, the state-file store into src/disk. Repo-approval cases move
to test/unit over the fake. Ten files leave FS_READERS; Config gets an
import rule.
